title: HAP1 cell line HAP_1_S47266
characteristics_ch1: cell type: control cell line
treatment_protocol_ch1: JQ12 (Siliphaivanh et al., 2007; Stiff et al., 2016) 1 μM, MS-275 (S1053, Selleck Chemicals) 3 μM, both 24 hours
growth_protocol_ch1: HAP1 cells were grown in IMDM+++ medium (IMDM (12440053, Thermo Scientific), supplemented with Penicillin-Streptomycin (P4333, Sigma-Aldrich, 1% final concentration) and fetal bovine serum (F7524, Sigma-Aldrich, 10% final concentration)) at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
extract_protocol_ch1: Total RNA from knockout (KO) and inactive mutant expressing cells, as well as inhibitor-treated cells (JQ12 1 μM, MS-275 3 μM, both 24 hours) was isolated using Trizol reagent (Thermo Fisher Scientific) as described in the manual. The isolated RNA, dissolved in nuclease-free ddH2O, was then subjected to another precipitation step by adding 1/10 vol. 3 M sodium-acetate (pH 5.2) and 2.5 vol. 96% ethanol. Following overnight-incubation, the samples were centrifuged (12000 rpm, 30 min, 4 °C) and washed with 75% ethanol. Pellets were air-dried and dissolved in a suitable amount of nuclease-free ddH2O (shaking at 300 rpm, 10 min, 55 °C).; RNA-seq libraries were prepared with the TruSeq Stranded mRNA LT sample preparation kit (Illumina) using Sciclone and Zephyr liquid handling robotics (PerkinElmer). Library amounts were quantified using the Qubit 2.0 Fluorometric Quantitation system (Life Technologies) and the size distribution was assessed using the Experion Automated Electrophoresis System (Bio-Rad). For sequencing, libraries were pooled, diluted and sequenced on an Illumina HiSeq 3000 instrument using 50 bp single-read chemistry.
data_processing: Illumina HiSeq Control Software (HCS) HD 3.4.0.38 was used for the data acquisition on the sequencing instrument.; On-instrument base-calling performed by the Illumina Real-Time Analysis (RTA) software 2.7.7.; BCL to BAM file conversion and demultiplexing with custom programmes (https://github.com/epigen/picard) based on Picard tools 2.19.2 (http://broadinstitute.github.io/picard/); Spliced genome alignments to GRCh38 (UCSC Genome Browser hg38) and Ensembl reference transcriptome e100 (April 2020) with STAR 2.7.5a and options suggested be the ENCODE project (--alignIntronMax 1000000 --alignIntronMin 20 --alignMatesGapMax 1000000 --alignSJDBoverhangMin 1 --alignSJoverhangMin 8 --outFilterMismatchNmax 999 --outFilterMismatchNoverReadLmax 0.04 --outFilterMultimapNmax 20 --outFilterType BySJout); Differential expression modelling with Bioconductor 3.12 package DESeq2 1.30.0, running under R 4.0.0.; Genome_build: GRCh38 (hg38) Reference Genome Assembly; Supplementary_files_format_and_content: Per gene and sample raw (integer) counts and DESeq2-calculated FPKMs in tab-separated value (TSV) format
contact_laboratory: Division of Cell and Developmental Biology
contact_department: Center for Anatomy and Cell Biology

growth_protocol_ch1: HAP1 cells were grown in IMDM+++ medium (IMDM (12440053, Thermo Scientific), supplemented with Penicillin-Streptomycin (P4333, Sigma-Aldrich, 1% final concentration) and fetal bovine serum (F7524, Sigma-Aldrich, 10% final concentration)) at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
extract_protocol_ch1: Total RNA from knockout (KO) and inactive mutant expressing cells, as well as inhibitor-treated cells (JQ12 1 μM, MS-275 3 μM, both 24 hours) was isolated using Trizol reagent (Thermo Fisher Scientific) as described in the manual. The isolated RNA, dissolved in nuclease-free ddH2O, was then subjected to another precipitation step by adding 1/10 vol. 3 M sodium-acetate (pH 5.2) and 2.5 vol. 96% ethanol. Following overnight-incubation, the samples were centrifuged (12000 rpm, 30 min, 4 °C) and washed with 75% ethanol. Pellets were air-dried and dissolved in a suitable amount of nuclease-free ddH2O (shaking at 300 rpm, 10 min, 55 °C).; RNA-seq libraries were prepared with the TruSeq Stranded mRNA LT sample preparation kit (Illumina) using Sciclone and Zephyr liquid handling robotics (PerkinElmer). Library amounts were quantified using the Qubit 2.0 Fluorometric Quantitation system (Life Technologies) and the size distribution was assessed using the Experion Automated Electrophoresis System (Bio-Rad). For sequencing, libraries were pooled, diluted and sequenced on an Illumina HiSeq 3000 instrument using 50 bp single-read chemistry.
